77685-legends-of-the-conquest-of-spain.title: Conquest Of Spain.
77685-legends-of-the-conquest-of-spain.creator: The Author Of “The Sketch-Book.”
77685-legends-of-the-conquest-of-spain.description: A book by The Author Of “The Sketch-Book.”. Hence the earliest chronicles which treat of the downfall of Spain are apt to be tinctured with those saintly miracles which savour of the pious labours of the cloister, or those fanciful fictions that betray their Arabian authors. Yet, from these apocryphal sources, the most legitimate and accredited Spanish histories have taken their rise, as pure rivers may be traced up to the fens and mantled pools of a morass.

arxiv-2302-07290.title: A Flexible Multi-Metric Bayesian Framework for Decision-Making in Phase II Multi-Arm Multi-Stage Studies
arxiv-2302-07290.creator: Suzanne M. Dufault, Angela M. Crook, Katie Rolfe, Patrick P. J. Phillips
arxiv-2302-07290.description: Abstract We propose a multi-metric flexible Bayesian framework to support efficient interim decision-making in multi-arm multi-stage phase II clinical trials. Multi-arm multi-stage phase II studies increase the efficiency of drug development, but early decisions regarding the futility or desirability of a given arm carry considerable risk since sample sizes are often low and follow-up periods may be short.

arxiv-2403-02642.title: UFO: Uncertainty-aware LiDAR-image Fusion for Off-road Semantic Terrain Map Estimation
arxiv-2403-02642.creator: Ohn Kim, Junwon Seo, Seongyong Ahn, Chong Hui Kim
arxiv-2403-02642.description: Abstract Autonomous off-road navigation requires an accurate semantic understanding of the environment, often converted into a bird’s-eye view (BEV) representation for various downstream tasks. While learning-based methods have shown success in generating local semantic terrain maps directly from sensor data, their efficacy in off-road environments is hindered by challenges in accurately representing uncertain terrain features.

arxiv-2412-06932.title: Families of Discrete Breathers on a Nonlinear Kagome Lattice
arxiv-2412-06932.creator: Andrew Hofstrand
arxiv-2412-06932.description: Abstract The unique geometry of the two-dimensional tripartite Kagome lattice is responsible for shaping diverse families of spatially localized and time-periodic nonlinear modes known as discrete breathers. We state conditions for the existence of breathers and compute their spatiotemporal profiles near the edges of the linear phonon spectrum.

arxiv-2501-15766.title: On Virial Expansion in Hard Sphere Model
arxiv-2501-15766.creator: Kiyoharu Kawana
arxiv-2501-15766.description: Abstract Virial expansion is a traditional approach in statistical mechanics that expresses thermodynamic quantities, such as pressure p p , as power series of density or chemical potential. Its radius of convergence can serve as a potential indicator of phase transition.

arxiv-2509-15102.title: Zero Indirect Band Gap in Non-Hermitian Systems
arxiv-2509-15102.creator: Rahul S, Giandomenico Palumbo
arxiv-2509-15102.description: Abstract Zero indirect gaps in band models are typically viewed as unstable and achievable only through fine-tuning. Recent works, however, have revealed robust semimetallic phases in Hermitian systems where the indirect gap remains pinned at zero over a finite parameter range. Here, we extend this paradigm to non-Hermitian lattice models by studying a one-dimensional diamond-like system with gain and loss.

arxiv-2511-09337.title: TempoQL: A Readable, Precise, and Portable Query System for Electronic Health Record Data
arxiv-2511-09337.creator: Ziyong Ma, Richard D. Boyce, Adam Perer, Venkatesh Sivaraman
arxiv-2511-09337.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ziyong Ma, Richard D. Boyce, Adam Perer, Venkatesh Sivaraman. Electronic health record (EHR) data is an essential data source for machine learning for health, but researchers and clinicians face steep barriers in extracting and validating EHR data for modeling. Existing tools incur trade-offs between expressivity and usability and are typically specialized to a single data standard, making it difficult to write temporal queries that are ready for modern model-building pipelines and adaptable to new datasets.

pmc-13029353.title: Body Composition and Dietary Intake of Combat Sports Athletes: A Systematic Review
pmc-13029353.creator: José Francisco Herrero Barceló, José Miguel Martínez Sanz, Mónica Castillo Martínez
pmc-13029353.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Combat sports are characterised by successive high-intensity and short-duration episodes (rounds) interspersed with short rest periods (intermittent nature). Athletes’ body composition and dietary intake are closely related to physiological demands, and they are determining factors in athletic performance. The aim of this systematic review was to describe the body composition, dietary intake, and food habits of male and female combat sports athletes, and to verify whether they met nutritional recommendations.

pmc-13108131.title: Functional Biomechanical Analysis of Javelin Throw Technique in Junior Athletes
pmc-13108131.creator: Ligia Cuciorovschi, Denisa-Iulia Brus, Ștefan Teriș, Răzvan Sandu Enoiu
pmc-13108131.description: Background: Javelin throw performance is strongly influenced by the coordination of the kinetic chain and by key biomechanical parameters related to technique execution. Understanding the functional biomechanical characteristics of javelin throw technique in junior athletes is essential for optimizing performance. Methods: This study investigated the biomechanical characteristics of javelin throw technique in junior athletes using an applied motion analysis approach.

pmc-13183893.title: Roles of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) in the pathogenesis of diabetic kidney disease (DKD)
pmc-13183893.creator: Zhi Zheng, Yunkuo Li, Yujie Pan
pmc-13183893.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a prevalent microvascular complication of diabetes, is a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. Moreover, it plays a crucial role in the morbidity and mortality of diabetic patients. Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), members of the nuclear hormone receptor superfamily, are key regulators of energy homeostasis, with three distinct subtypes identified: PPARα, PPARγ, and PPARβ/δ. They regulate gene transcription associated with energy metabolism, differentiation, inflammation, and cellular development.

pmc-13217022.title: Aggravation of rainbow sign on hematoma membrane by arterial spin labeling predicts chronic subdural hematoma recurrence following middle meningeal artery embolization

pmc-13217022.description: BackgroundRecurrence remains a critical challenge in patients with chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) treated with middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE), yet the underlying mechanisms and reliable predictors of this phenomenon remain poorly understood. Current predictors of recurrence rely on invasive or radiation-based techniques, prompting the need for non-invasive imaging markers.

Although stellate ganglion block (SGB) can modulate sympathetic tone and inflammatory reactions, its efficacy in preventing DLT-related POST is still inconclusive.
